guidance.heading: Guidance
section: Cisco expects to achieve the following results for the second quarter of fiscal 2027:

Revenue | $18.0 billion - $18.2 billion
Non-GAAP gross margin | 65% - 66%
Non-GAAP operating margin | 36% - 37%
Non-GAAP EPS | $1.34 - $1.36
Cisco estimates that GAAP EPS will be $1.07 to $1.09 for the second quarter of fiscal 2027.
Cisco expects to achieve the following results for fiscal 2027:
Cisco estimates that GAAP EPS will be $4.38 to $4.44 for fiscal 2027.

Our Q2 FY 2027 guidance assumes an effective tax provision rate of approximately 14.5% for GAAP and approximately 18.5% for non-GAAP results. Our FY 2027 guidance assumes an effective tax provision rate of approximately 16% for GAAP and approximately 18.5% for non-GAAP results.

A reconciliation between the guidance on a GAAP and non-GAAP basis is provided in the tables entitled “GAAP to non-GAAP Guidance” located in the section entitled “Reconciliations of GAAP to non-GAAP Measures.”

desk.headline: Revenue up 24% to a record $18.5bn and adjusted EPS $1.40, both beat; full-year FY27 revenue and EPS outlook raised
results: Sales jumped 24% to a record $18.5bn, Cisco's fastest growth in over 15 years; product sales rose 32% while services grew just 1%.
Networking was the engine, up 43% to $11.1bn; Security rose 7%, Collaboration 8% and Observability 2%. All three regions grew double digits, led by the Americas (+28%).
Adjusted EPS rose 40% to $1.40 and GAAP EPS 58% to $1.14; revenue, adjusted operating margin and adjusted EPS all came in above the top of Cisco's own guidance.
Gross margin slipped (non-GAAP 65.6% from 68.1%) as more hardware was sold, but tight cost control lifted operating margin to a record 37.8%.
$3.7bn went back to shareholders ($2.0bn buybacks, $1.7bn dividends); $6.1bn of buyback authority remains and the $0.42 quarterly dividend was declared again.

guidance.summary: Cisco raised its full-year FY27 outlook to $74.8–75.8bn revenue (from $72.2–73.4bn) and $5.47–5.53 adjusted EPS (from $5.05–5.11). For the December quarter it expects $18.0–18.2bn revenue and $1.34–1.36 adjusted EPS. It also lifted its FY27 target for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9bn, from $7.5bn.

points: Management called this the early stage of a multi-year networking 'supercycle' driven by AI, campus refreshes and sovereign data centres.
Total orders rose 21% (14% excluding hyperscalers); service provider and cloud orders were up 47%, enterprise 15% and public sector 13%.
Three new AI design wins in the quarter; the $9bn hyperscaler AI target excludes neocloud customers, whose credit exposure was called relatively small.

Higher memory and component costs plus a heavier hardware mix are squeezing gross margin; price rises and long-term supply deals are offsetting part of it, with full-year adjusted gross margin seen just under 65%.
Only a small share of switches sold so far are the new models, which management presented as a sign the campus upgrade cycle has a long way to run.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance and 24/7 Wall St., 12 Nov 2026 (prepared remarks not in the filing)

watch: Whether price rises keep pace with memory and component costs as gross margin trends toward 65%.
Progress toward the $9bn hyperscaler AI revenue target and how lumpy those large orders are.
Whether Security growth picks up later in the year, as management expects.
